TOMATO-PASTE-PUREE-ALIAS (tomato-24b; counted separately, not a head): identity from FSSAI Food Product Standards Chapter 2.3 clause 2.3.14 "Thermally Processed Tomato Puree and Paste" (https://www.fssai.gov.in/docs/food-law/regulations/compendium/food-products-standards/Chapter%202_3_Fruit_Vegetable_products.pdf): "obtained by concentrating the juice of sound ripe tomatoes to the desired concentration. It may contain salt and other ingredients suitable to the products"; tomato puree (total soluble solids not less than 9.0 percent) and tomato paste (not less than 25 percent) are the two named products. Codex CXS 57-1981 Processed Tomato Concentrates likewise designates tomato puree and tomato paste as tomato concentrate (https://www.fao.org/input/download/standards/237/CXS_057e.pdf). Recognition routing only: the tomato concentrate row's placement (Brazil Dietary Guidelines Group 3 clause for tomato extract or concentrates with salt and/or sugar) and its rule apply unchanged: Group 3 only when salt or sugar is stated and nothing else is listed or bracketed; otherwise abstain; never Group 1 for the bare term. Scope: only tomato paste is aliased. FSSAI 2.3.14 and Codex both put paste at 25 percent soluble solids or more, which is always a concentrate. Tomato puree is NOT aliased: the clause covers only the thermally processed puree (9.0 percent or more), a label does not say whether a listed puree meets that, and a fresh blended puree is not a concentrate, so adding salt to the bare word would place a food the evidence does not cover. Tomato puree stays unrecognised until a label states a concentrate.
